page.layout: One page of text. Above the text, two medallion engravings side by side (left: portrait of two men; right: portrait of a bust). Running head at the top centre, page number at the top right. Signature at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: IOANNES Palæologus,dictus etiam Calo-ioannes,patri Andronico iuniori succedit,licet Ioannes Cantacuzenus,tutor prudens,imperium administret Constantinopolitanum circa annum mundi 5290. à Christo nato 1328. Tutor itaque Can-tacuzenus,ac imperij consors Apocauci fraude (viri quidem obscuri,sed solertis & callidi,ac inter principis amicos ob eiusmodi mores,præcipuæ dignationis) & Patriarchæ ambitione,in exilium truditur. iniuriæ impatiens bellum quinquennale aduersus Reginam & Ioannem Cantacuzenum Imperatorem,Andronici filium gerit,Turcarum arma Europæ primus infert. Huic tandem proditur Byzantium:quod cum occupasset,nulli molestus fuit,imperij tantum consortem egit,filia in vxorem Ioanni tradita. Inde in Genuenses,sociis Venetis & Arrago-niis,varia fortuna bellum gerit Cantacuzenus:cui & statim ab Ioanne Palæologo exule prædicto bellum indictum,Turcarum in primis ope geritur,quibus etiam in Europa locum primum inhabitandum tradidit. Cum autem improuisus Byzantium,ex Tenedo soluens,ingressus esset Palæologus,tandem Canta-cuzenus imperio relicto,monachum egit. Palæologus Mat-thæum Cantacuzeni filium participe imperij agere volentem,imperium deponere coëgit. & cum multa bella confecisset Palæologus,moriens filio Manueli imperiu reliquit. Vide Egnat. lib.2.& Cofm.Mun.lib.4.
MANVEL prædicti Ioannis Palæologi filius,post patrem imperat Constantinopoli: septem mares filios hic reliquit,quorum Ioannes natu maximus,morienti successit. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: Medallion engravings above the text carry legends: left medallion "IO. CAN." and "IOAN. PALAEOL."; right medallion "MANV" and "EL. II" (partly legible, read from the illustration, not transcribed into the text). Scan is slightly grey; "imperiu" and "Cofm" are read as printed and may be doubtful. The left-hand word "Arrago-" is read as printed and may be doubtful.
